facts.fact: On 5 September 2019 the plenary of the national validation workshop (3-5 September, held under the Head of State's patronage) adopted the amended Draft Zéro of the Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025 by show of hands and unanimously, and the plan is stated to be validated by all stakeholders; the Special Adviser handed it to the Minister of PTNTIC, representing the President, who took note and promised to send it on to the Government; the document names no cabinet adoption and no enacting decree.

The document is the full text of the plan, dated September 2019 and issued under the Presidency's copyright, with its source URL on the Presidency's own site (presidence.cd); it covers four pillars (infrastructure, content, application uses, governance and regulation) and, among other things, the digital transformation of administrations and enterprises.
The plan states that it carries the national digital development strategy to the horizon 2025, with intermediate target years of 2020 to 2025 in its priority-action timetable.

Chapter 5 of the plan gives a timetable of 68 priority projects with indicators, baseline and target values (targets dated 2020 to 2025), a priority rank and responsible entities, and appendix 3 is a dashboard of objectives and actions by pillar; the budget-estimate column carries no figures, the note beneath it stating that the workshop panellists left the Government and the ADN to evaluate budgets, and the plan lists drawing up an action plan on the ADN's proposal and a financing plan as actions still to be done.

The plan states that the organising committee of the validation workshop, created by Decision 19/077 of the Head of State's Cabinet Director (dated 10 August in the front matter and 19 August in chapter 2 and the bibliography), will follow up validation and implementation until the structures to be created are in place; the Conseil National du Numérique and the Agence de Développement du Numérique are described as bodies still to be created, the ADN by Prime Minister's decree targeted for 2020.

The plan states no budget line or cost for itself: its budget-estimate column is blank, the panellists left the evaluation of budgets to the Government and the ADN, and it lists a financing plan for the plan's actions as a task to be drawn up, while the Head of State calls for financing beyond the Treasury, including public-private partnerships.
